newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on gov't cool-off moves.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on gov't cool-off moves.

text.p: Late profit-taking on electronics eroded early gains and sent Taiwan share prices to a lower close on Thursday amid caution after the government's persistent moves to cool the red-hot stock market, brokers said.

The index surged to a seven-year intraday high 9,045.35, eclisping last week's 9,021.87 benchmark, but slipped sharply near the close to end at 8,871.76 -- a loss of 84.65 points or 0.95 percent compared to Wednesday.
Brokers said investors turned cautious after the finance ministry said on Wednesday it had no immediate plans to raise the ceiling on foreign ownership of Taiwan stocks.
Separately, the watchdog Securities and Futures Commission said on Wednesday it had launched what it called a routine probe into credit trading practices in the stock market.
The commission denied the move aimed to cool down the red-hot stock market, though analysts said it had that effect.
"Bullish sentiment has gradually cooled off following the government's repeated moves to chill the market," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.
Thursday's turnover was extremely heavy at T$232.2 billion, the market's third highest in history. Last Thursday, turnover spiked to an all-time-high T$251 billion.
Electronics surged more than two percent in early trade but suffered late profit-taking to end at 0.04 percent lower.
Taiwan Semiconductor was down T$4.5 to T$120. But computer giant Acer surged T$6.5 to T$107.5.

Chipmaker Winbond was up the daily seven percent limit to T$58.5 after confimring it was considering investing in a huge wafer project worth around T$160 billion in the island's burgeoning southern Tainan science park.
Brokers attributed the market's downturn in part to rising caution ahead of Hong Kong's handover to China on July 1.
